page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: uno incepta, Physicis Astronomicisq; inpri-mis gaudens, quæ deinde per & post Socratem, in utramque partem disputantem, phy-ficaq; studia in Ethica permutantem, in duas hasce præcipuas sectas( Cynica & Epicurea[?] subito sublatis ) Academicam Platonis, & Stoicam Zenonis est divisa: ex quibus Academica Peripateticam ab Aristotele Platonis discipulo ortam genuit: Stoica vero jamdiu fere evanuit.
Latini phi-losophiæ fe-ctarii.Latini philosophi præteritis poëtis fue-runt partim Academici, partim Stoici.

In Academicis præcipuus fuit Cicero.Stoici Tractatus authoris de philosophiâ veterum & recentiorū.Cato & Seneca, aliiq;, de quibus agimus in no-stră philosophiâ veterum & recentiorum; ubi modum docendi, qui inde ab Adamo, ad hæc nostra tempora apud singulas obtinuit sectas, percenfe-mus.
Philosophi recentiores suntSequuntur sectæ philosophorum recen-tiores. Philosophi recentiores sunt Christia-niilli[?], qui post Christum floruerunt.
Suntq;, vel minus, vel magis recentes.
Minùs recentes sunt Patres Ecclesiastici, & Doctores Scholastici.

I.Patres Ec-clesiastici.Patres Ecclesiastici sunt vel Græci, vel Latini, qui Christianam philosophiam adver-sus Gentiles afferuerunt, ejusq; usum in Ec-clesiâ monstrârunt. Tales sunt cumprimis, Damascenus, Chrysostomus, Augustinus, Justinus Martyr & philosophus, Irenæus, Lactantiuus, Clemens Alexandrinus, Tertul-lianus.

page.notes: Printed page with one main column and right-hand marginal notes. Doubtful readings: "Epicurea" (a mark may be present over the final vowel); "Christia-niilli" (the word break and the spacing of "ni illi" are unclear). The printed "funt" in the margin and the main text is read as "sunt", since the long s is set as f-like in this face. The "I." in the margin is a bare numeral placed beside the paragraph, and is given as a note.
